To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the area function of two convex polygons is a polynomial function of their relative positions and that its minimum is attained at a contact configuration that is a real solution of a system of quadratic equations.
the contact configurations between two convex polygons have algebraic structures and that these algebraic structures are crucial for finding minimum area convex packings.

(i) there is an O((n +m)nm) time algorithm for finding a global minimum area convex packing; (ii) the search space is discretized using the algebraic structure of contact configurations; and (iii) the algorithm is designed to exploit the algebraic structure and the geometric properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design of a new efficient algorithm for a fundamental geometric packing problem that has remained open for over 20 years, and the algorithmic design is motivated by a careful study of the underlying geometry and algebra of the problem.
the design and analysis of a novel algorithmic framework for solving the problem of finding a minimum area packing of two convex shapes in the plane.
the design and analysis of a deterministic algorithm for the Minimum Area Convex Packing Problem.
